system.summary: Numeric groups of 2-4 digits separated by full stops, set inside clear letters. Most groups split into two numbers of 2-24 (2210 = 22|10, 912 = 9|12); the editors of 1824 printed them as figures because they had no key.
system.notes: Same system in both writers' letters (shared groups 199, 515, 129, 814, 1220), so it is probably Duplessis's cipher with his Paris correspondents in 1593.

prior_solution.where: Brice Dudout, Europe chiffrée (bdudout.github.io/europe-chiffree/en/documents.html#mornay-1593), published Oct 2026 after this project's transcription and failed attempt; key built on P1-P5 and S1, P6 and S2 held out.

conditions.human_role: Asked for a target that needs no archive request; chose this one.

solution.what: Searched the full text of all 12 volumes (archive.org) for chiffre/déchiffré and runs of figures. Mme de Rohan's 1594 letter (vol. 6 LVI) is printed with its decipherment above the figures; Du Maurier and Serviez 1593 (vol. 5), Loménie 24 Feb 1595 (vol. 6 CVII) and Duplessis 1597-98 (vols. 7-8) are printed as bare figures.
Transcribed the eight 1593 passages (93 groups, 62 distinct) from the page images with their clear context (ciphertext.txt).
Split each group into two numbers of 1-24; both halves draw on the same set of values, suggesting each half stands for a letter (a bigram per group).

anneal_pairs.py: number->letter key annealed onto fr-1600-letters (order 4, no spaces) with a French letter-frequency penalty, 10 restarts. No restart produced French; the bigram-per-group reading is not supported at this length.

Built the Mme de Rohan 1594 key (78 values) from the decipherment printed above her figures, vol. 6 pp. 83-85 (rohan1594_key.tsv): letters 6-65, syllables 88-175, word codes 660-919 including 810 = de and 910 = les, and names 10 = le roi, 87 = Paris, 95 = Tours, 96 = Saumur.

Transcribed Loménie to Duplessis, 24 Feb 1595 (15 passages, vol. 6 pp. 179-181), Duplessis to his wife 1595 (vol. 6 p. 182) and Duplessis to Cargroy and to his wife, 18-19 Jan 1597 (11 passages, vol. 7 pp. 124-126) from the page images.

Applied the Rohan 1594 key to the 1595 and 1597 figures. The output does not make French: most groups have no value, and those that do give place names and letters in the middle of words. The key is not the one used in these letters. One partial fit: in Loménie, 'du sieur 810 62 110 4' reads as 'du sieur de ...', so the word-code series ending in 10 may be shared even though the letter values differ.

Brice Dudout (email of 27 Oct 2026, Europe chiffrée) read the 1593 figures: two letters per group, as hypothesis A said, but on a folded alphabet: a = 2, then c-m on rising odd numbers 5-21, n-u on falling even numbers 22-8, 44 = x/y; 1 and 3 never occur, b unattested. His key (key_dudout.tsv) applied to this project's transcription by apply_dudout.py: 93/93 groups give letters; three groups split two ways (219 me/al, 213 an/na, 215 ah/mc) and the sense picks one each time. P1 reads "l'arrest estoit adresse contre le duc de Guise pour le tirer a quatre chevaux", S2 "le roy est trahi". The anneal of step 2 had the right unit but not the key.

Dudout froze the key on P1-P5 and S1 and read P6 and S2 without change (7.6 sd above 2,000 permuted keys, per his page). Our transcription gives the same text letter for letter except P1 'larest' (his 'l'arrest') and S1 'lenteprinse' (his 'l'entreprinse'): either a dropped group in the print or his normalisation; to check on the page image.
Dudout's second email: no group is missing in P1/S1. The cipher gives "larest" and "lenteprinse"; his "l'arrest" and "l'entreprinse" are the normalised spelling of the established text.

Transcribed the remaining bare figures of vols. 7-8 from the archive.org page images (beling/transcription/v7v8_figures.tsv, clear context in a separate file): Mme de Rohan to Mme Duplessis, 27 Feb and 4 Aug 1597 (19 passages, 50 groups), and Duplessis to his wife, Sep 1597-Apr 1598 (15 passages, 79 groups) (Andrew Beling, beling/).

Pre-registered test (beling/PREREG.md) of Dudout's folded 1593 key on Lomenie 1595 and Duplessis Jan 1597 (203 groups): coverage 0.655 vs best 0.616 of 200 random number sets (pass needed 0.85, margin 0.30); language score -3.43 per letter, beats 193/200 permuted keys, vs -2.24 on the 1593 control. Inconclusive by the rule; the output makes no words. Shifted keys (c = 1-100) give nothing (Andrew Beling, beling/).
Pre-registered test of the Rohan 1594 key on Mme de Rohan's 1597 figures (50 groups): coverage 0.78, -2.26 per letter, beats 197/200 permuted keys. Fits (small sample) (Andrew Beling, beling/).

Rohan 1597 runs read from the 1594 key plus four inferred values (672 = roy, 134 = lo, 38 = g, 160 = ro): 'M. de Villeroy et de Lomenie', 'M. de Cargrois', 'M. de Chastillon' (one sign off), 'le roy'. Two runs not read. Inferred values untested (beling/results/rohan1597_reading.md) (Andrew Beling, beling/).

Searched vols. 9-12 for bare figures (OCR of both scans, then page images): Duplessis to his wife Jan-Mar 1599 (30 groups), Mme de Rohan to Duplessis 1599 (4) and Nov 1611-Mar 1612 (84), unsigned letter of 25 Jul 1612 (9); none in vols. 10 and 12. Also the twelve places of the name code 81 63 in vol. 8 (beling/transcription/v9v12_figures.tsv, v8_namecode.tsv) (Andrew Beling, beling/).

Pre-registered (beling/PREREG_round2.md): the Rohan 1594 key on Mme de Rohan's 1599 and 1611-12 figures (88 groups): coverage 0.57, -2.69 per letter, beats 85/200 permuted keys; does not fit (another table by 1611). The round-1 inferred values: only 38 recurs (once); extended key beats 130/200 random-value controls; not supported (Andrew Beling, beling/).

Searched for a clear copy of the 1595-99 figures (archive.org, the 1625 edition, web): none. Cribs for Lomenie 24 Feb 1595: the editors' note under the letter (the sieur de Camor's plan against Mercoeur) and the king's same-day cipher letter printed in clear (vol. 6 CVI) (Andrew Beling, beling/).

The cribs make 'du sieur 810 62 110 4' = 'du sieur de Camor' and '810 44 109 27 32 10' = 'de Bretagne' likely; not a key. Lomenie's x10 codes (23/95) are nearly absent from Duplessis's own letters (4/239): probably two systems (beling/results/explore_system.txt, README section 6.5) (Andrew Beling, beling/).

Integration check of PR #449: test_folded.py and test_round2.py re-run on the archive.org vol. 6 OCR (sha256 204906c7... matches): T1 folded 1593 key on Lomenie 1595 + Duplessis 1597 coverage 0.655 against best 0.616 (inconclusive; no words), T2 Rohan 1594 key on Rohan 1597 coverage 0.78 and language beats 197/200 (fits, 50 groups), T3 Rohan key on 1599-1612 does not fit, T4 inferred values not supported; all identical. Strictly, only 4 of the 50 Rohan 1597 groups read without an inferred value or a name-code letter; read share recounted 0.182, not 0.247. No second decoder and no image check at the integration check.

Read share measured over cipher words only (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026) on beling/reading_1593.md, per letter section: the **bold** deciphered passages counted, the printed clear words around them left out; holes by words with the v2_score rules (apostrophe words as one). Du Maurier P1-P6: 28 of 29 (Tour[ay]ne a hole), 0.966; Serviez S1-S2: 6 of 7, 0.857 (l'entreprinse a hole: the figures give 'lenteprinse', the r supplied; l'arrest for 'larest' a period spelling, read). Neither had a read share (the file scored whole, notes included, gives 0.994). Du Maurier stays read; Serviez read -> read in part; Rohan 1597 (not prose) not measured; class read in part unchanged (fraction_read 0.182 of groups).

Coordinator's decisions (16 Nov 2026): l'arrest stays read (period spelling 'larest'), l'entreprinse stays a hole (the writer's omission, gap reworded); words resting on a probable value count as holes, so chevaux (sign 44 = x/y, probable) joins Tour[ay]ne. Du Maurier 0.966 -> 0.931, read -> read in part; Serviez 0.857 unchanged. Class read in part unchanged.

Full-texts audit: the seven documents that are not read (Loménie 1595, Duplessis 1597, 1597-98 and 1599, Rohan 1599 and 1611-12, unsigned 1612) listed in outcome.texts with their transcriptions and the pre-registered mechanical decodes already in beling/results (mechanical.txt, round2_mechanical.txt), state decoded, not read. No new decode was run and no file changed.

Shawn Grening (grening/): Loménie 1595 from Andrew Beling's two cribs (step 8). With 10 read as one figure, 810 62 110 4 is seven figures for 'de Camor' and 810 44 109 27 32 10 is eleven for 'de Bretaigne' (the king's spelling in CVI). They give a 2, b 4, c 6, d 8, e 10: one figure 1-10 per letter, two letters per group, the alphabet folded onto the ten figures (a-e 2-10 even, f-l 1-9 odd, m n 1 2, o-s 10-2 even, t-z 9-1 odd). 13 of the 15 passages then encode exactly to the printed figures (158 letters): province de Bretaigne, de Camor, les despesches, de Vennes, ville de seureté de Bretaigne, la necessité, d'edicts, l'assamblée de Saumur, Bearn, la messe, de Boisdauphin, le marquis de Belisle. L8 'du roy' is doubtful (print has 8, the rule gives y = 3, y occurs nowhere else); L15 reads '[...] querelles'. Each figure stands for two or three letters; f, x, z are inferred.

grening/scripts/test_key.py, written after the reading (not pre-registered). Letter trigrams from the vol. 6 OCR with CVI, CVII and the table of contents cut out. The twelve crib letters fixed; the other ten by the folded-alphabet rule or at random: on the passages the cribs do not touch (130 figures) the rule scores -2.045 per figure against 2,000 random keys (mean -2.282, sd 0.060, best -2.106), beating 2,000 of 2,000, z = 3.9.

grening/scripts/test_key.py --anneal: twelve annealing runs from random keys on all fifteen passages, no cribs. They reach -1.947 to -2.080 per figure (1-4 letters per figure) and -1.985 to -2.087 (2-3 letters); the pattern key scores -2.050, and no run agrees with it on more than 10 of 18 attested letters. On 163 figures a letter model cannot pick out a polyphonic key: the cribs are needed. docs/_validate.py does not apply (polyphonic).
The same split and key on Duplessis's figures of Jan 1597 (duplessis1597.txt): no words, three bare 0 figures, too many 5s. Looked at, not scored. The key is Loménie's, not Duplessis's.

Shawn Grening (grening/README_1597.md): Duplessis to Cargroy, 19 Jan 1597 (C1-C8). Hypothesis after the Loménie key: the same method (one figure 1-10 per letter, two letters per group) with the alphabet in order, which leaves ten tables. With a = 7 (a 7, b 8, c 9, d 10, e 1 ...) six of the eight passages encode exactly to the printed figures (132 of 155 figures): C2 'un prisonnier de qualite', C3 'pour signal une eguillete bleue au pourpoint ou a la mandille', C4 'vos gens de Poitou dient', C6 'Courbejoliere', C7 'ruine sur sa maison', C8 'Monbarot'. An odd number of letters is filled with a final e (last group 11). C1 reads 'du part.. contrai' with 11 where 'parti' wants 5; C5 (eight figures) is not read. f, h, x, y, z inferred. No crib; both names occur in clear elsewhere in vol. 7. The transcription is the repo's, compared with the page images of pp. 124-126.

grening/scripts/test_key_1597.py, written after the reading (not pre-registered); letter trigrams from the vol. 6 OCR. Ten rotations on all passages: a = 7 scores -2.222 per figure, the other nine -2.753 to -3.128. Held-out: with the twelve letters of Courbejoliere and Monbarot fixed, the alphabetical rule beats 2,000 of 2,000 random fillings of the other ten letters on C2, C3, C4 and C7 (z = 2.2). Annealing from random keys with no cribs: 5 of 24 runs score a little above the key with other tables, so a letter model alone does not single it out among all tables; among the ten of the hypothesis it does. docs/_validate.py does not apply (polyphonic).

The letter to his wife of the same days (W1-W3: 40, 80, 132, letters printed among the figures) is another system; neither ten-figure table was fitted to it. Loménie's folded table and its ten shifts give no words on C1-C8.

gaps.detail: 'du roy' fits, but the print has 8 where the folded-alphabet rule gives y = 3, and y occurs nowhere else in the letter. The manuscript would show whether the figure is 3 or 8.
100 holds the only 0 that is not part of a 10; perhaps a name figure like the 98 and 99 in the clear text. Two groups, one occurrence.

gaps.item: Lomenie 1595 name figures in the clear text (3, 11, 14, 16, 25, 26, 98, 99) and the letters f, x, z
gaps.detail: The name figures are a separate list the letter key says nothing about. f, x and z do not occur; their values are inferred from the pattern.

gaps.item: Duplessis to Cargroy Jan 1597, C1 (119 where 'parti' wants 5; 'contrai' without ending) and C5 (75 87 95 66)
gaps.detail: C1 reads 'du part.. contrai'; the group is a clear 119 in the print. C5, eight figures, gives no word with the key (a/m/y i/u b/n/z a/m/y c/o i/u l/x l/x). The manuscript would show whether the print's figures are right.

gaps.item: Duplessis's figures to his wife, Jan 1597 (W1-W3) and Sep 1597-1599 (about 130 groups)
gaps.detail: Another system (40, 80, 132, letters printed among the figures; name codes 81 63, 153 63, 33). Neither ten-figure letter table was fitted to them; the Sep 1597-1599 figures were not tried.
1594 key fits; 672, 134, 160 inferred and not seen again; 38 once more (1599), not supported; runs R1 and R18 not read.
Another table; the 1594 key does not fit (pre-registered, 12 Nov 2026).

gaps.item: Serviez S1, l'entreprinse: the cipher has no r (the figures give 'lenteprinse', no group missing, NOTES step 6)
gaps.detail: A letter the writer left out of the cipher: every sign that is there is read, and the missing letter cannot be recovered from any file here. Counted as a hole (16 Nov 2026). The checker offers no blocker type for letters left out; this is the nearest.
44 occurs only at the end of P1 and P2; values probable.

outcome.notes: 1593 part read via Dudout's key; 1595-98 open. 11-12 Nov 2026 (Andrew Beling, beling/): vols. 7-12 searched and their figures transcribed (six new documents); the Rohan 1594 key fits Mme de Rohan's 1597 letters but not her 1611-12 ones; Dudout's folded key does not fit 1595-97; the 1595-99 Duplessis/Lomenie figures stay unread. 12 Nov 2026 integration check: all tests re-run and reproduced (corpus hash matches); strict read share 0.182 (contributor's 0.247 counts name-code letters and inferred values); the Rohan 1594 key 'fits' Rohan 1597 on a small sample where only 'le roy' and 'Madame' read without inference. 27 Nov 2026 (Shawn Grening, grening/): Lomenie 1595 read in part with a ten-figure folded letter key built from Beling's two cribs; 13 of 15 passages exact. 28 Nov 2026 (Shawn Grening): Duplessis to Cargroy, 19 Jan 1597, read in part with the alphabet in order on ten figures (a = 7); 6 of 8 passages exact.
outcome.method_basis: 1593 Du Maurier/Serviez figures (93 groups) read with the key Brice Dudout published for them (27 Oct 2026), applied to this project's transcription; Loménie's letter of 1595 read in part (27 Nov 2026) with a ten-figure letter key built from two cribs taken from the clear text beside it and the king's letter of the same day; Duplessis's letter to Cargroy of Jan 1597 read in part (28 Nov 2026) with a second ten-figure letter key found from the ciphertext under the hypothesis of an alphabet in order; his figures to his wife remain not read.

texts.label: Du Maurier to Duplessis-Mornay, July 1593: six cipher passages P1-P6 (this project's transcription; Dudout's key, key_dudout.tsv)
texts.note: Brice Dudout's key applied to this project's transcription; 93/93 groups read. Word-divided reading and English translation added 12 Nov 2026 (beling/reading_1593.md, translation_1593.md); P1 corrected there to 'estoit ia dressé' (the figures), against 'estoit adressé' in NOTES step 6. 16 Nov 2026: read share over cipher words only 0.931: 27 of the 29 words in the six **bold** passages (P1-P6) of the Du Maurier section of beling/reading_1593.md. The two holes are the two words that use sign 44 (x/y), whose value is probable: Tour[ay]ne and chevaux (the x is unmarked in the reading and the only value that gives a word, but the sign's value is not attested; sure words only, coordinator's decision of 16 Nov 2026). l'arrest counts as read: the figures give 'larest', a spelling of the period, which the reading normalises. The printed clear words around the passages are left out. No read share had been recorded; the whole file, clear text and notes included, scores 0.994, not the measure. Read -> read in part.

texts.label: Loménie to Duplessis-Mornay, 24 Feb 1595: cipher runs L1-L15 (the D run, Duplessis to his wife, vol. 6 CIX, is not read)
texts.summary: Loménie, the king's secretary, answers Duplessis-Mornay on the day Henri IV wrote to him in cipher about the same affair (vol. 6 CVI): the sieur de Camor's offer in Brittany, for which he may be promised a town of surety there. The cipher also hides news from court: the need of the king's affairs, edicts sent for verification, the assembly of Saumur, the deputies of Béarn come about the mass, and the expected submission of Boisdauphin and the marquis de Belle-Île.
texts.note: Key grening/key_lomenie1595.tsv (27 Nov 2026, Shawn Grening, from Andrew Beling's cribs). 33 of 35 cipher words by the contributor's count of the bold words; the two holes are [?roy] (L8: the print has 8 where the rule gives y = 3) and the unread 100 76 before 'querelles' (L15), counted as one word, an estimate. Each figure stands for two or three letters, so the decryption file lists the letters each figure allows and the reading chooses among them. The reading holds the French sentences and the English translation in one file. Under the short-text floor (fewer than 40 cipher words, 2 holes) the entry could be 'read'; it is left 'read in part' for the reviewer. No reading_review yet. The D run on the last line of lomenie1595.txt is Duplessis's own cipher and is not read.

texts.label: Duplessis-Mornay to Cargroy, Saumur 19 Jan 1597: cipher runs C1-C8 (the W runs, to his wife, vol. 7 LXVII, are not read)
texts.summary: Duplessis-Mornay tells Cargroy that a friend, with a few men, will bring him a prisoner of quality to be taken on to Saumur by the king's express command, and gives the sign by which the man will be known: a blue lace on his doublet or coat. He also reports pressing for the upkeep of Cargroy's troop, suggests he take over the one granted to Courbejolière, who gave it up so as not to bring ruin on his house, and says he was glad to have met M. de Montbarot.
texts.note: Key grening/key_duplessis1597.tsv (28 Nov 2026, Shawn Grening): the alphabet in order on figures 1-10 starting at a = 7. 27 of 30 cipher words by the contributor's count of the bold words; the holes are [?parti] and [?contraire] in C1 (the print has 11 where 'parti' wants 5, and no ending) and the unread C5, counted as one word, an estimate. Each figure stands for two or three letters; the decryption file lists the letters each figure allows. The reading holds the French and the English in one file. No reading_review yet. The W runs of duplessis1597.txt (letter LXVII, to his wife) are another system and are not read.

outcome.fraction_read_source: 12 Nov 2026 integration recount, strict (README read bar: guessed, inferred and name-code letter values are holes): 534 code groups in all (1593: 93; Lomenie 1595: 95; Duplessis Jan 1597: 90; Rohan 1597: 50; Duplessis 1597-98: 79; Duplessis 1599: 30; Rohan 1599: 4; Rohan 1611-12: 84; unsigned 1612: 9). Read as sense: the 93 groups of 1593 (Dudout's key) and 4 of the 50 Rohan 1597 groups, the key's own values with no inference (10 = le roy in R10, R13, R15; 11 = Madame in R12); 97/534 = 0.182.
